title: The paradox of global poverty
body:
Conversation with a rider
with an employee
airport control:
-Sir you cannot pass through here (showing an empty passage to an empty xray).
You will have to pass through there (showing a crowded route).
-But the hallway is empty here.
-Yes, but this is fast lane. For riders who have paid.
-But no one is coming, we will facilitate the flow.
-That's the point of fast lane.
Unwittingly, the employee uttered a great truth.
And there I realized that fast lane is a service with, theoretically, huge risk.
The possibility that no one is going to fast lane
and everyone going to the other entrances
or the possibility of everyone going to fast lane,
both run the risk of losing their meaning.
Because "service" - air provided as a privilege,
when it becomes a privilege for everyone, then it is no longer.
It's not the fast lane,
are the privileges we think we are given.
It's all about balance.
In order to have fast lane,
no company wants all its passengers to endure it.
Paradox
85 — m
